args: Create a new skill "RepoPulse" for Azure DevOps repo analysis and work tracking. Purpose: on-demand analysis of ADO repos (org from ADO_ORG in ~/.claude/.env) producing Obsidian-format markdown with mermaid diagrams into ~/corpus/inform/Working_area/RepoAnalysis/. Two modes: (1) deep-dive on most active repos — shape, purpose, how work flows through them, change tracking over time to reveal working patterns; (2) cross-repo analysis — all repos, activity, intent, and the common thread in how work is conducted. Needs deterministic TypeScript tools for the ADO REST calls (repos, commits, PRs, contributors) so the model does analysis not plumbing. Work-confidential: output never goes to ~/obsidian.

args:
Three-section "What's in it for me?" one-pager for the Inform digital department's ways-of-working session. Audience: the digital team (Seán, Tom, Jake, Darragh, Archie, Shivani, Steve). Purpose: set the scene BEFORE any structure detail — reduce anxiety, answer "why are we doing this" and "what do I get".

All content must come from Erica Jefferies' and Dom's own words in the 10 Sept meeting (source: ~/corpus/inform/Working_area/Meetings/Erica_Dom_10_09_2026/Transcript.md). Verbatim quotes below.

SECTION 1 — WHERE WE'VE BEEN (history)
Erica: "we've evolved, we've grown up. We've evolved, we've grown in size."
The arc: a team that did internal IT.

SECTION 2 — WHERE WE ARE NOW (current state)
Erica, verbatim: "We deliver client work. We're asked to deliver what we call frontier firm technology. We continue to support the business. We've created additional tools for mod that might become products."
Also now live: a digital strategy and roadmap being kicked off, which the WHOLE team gets to input into — everyone will be asked what their biggest governance constraints are, "what keeps you up at night".
Erica's high-level statement of the shift: "taking us from a team that does internal IT to a capability that delivers engineering, quality engineering to clients. We are so much more than we were."

SECTION 3 — WHAT THE STRUCTURE MEANS FOR ME (WIIFM)
The reassurance, Dom's words: "this is not a regime change, this is just us getting better at what we're doing" — more predictable, more professional.
The principle, Dom's words: "guardrails rather than gates — enough structure to be predictable, professional, with the freedom to think, adapt and improve. We're not writing rules because people cannot be trusted. We're capturing what we have learned so nobody has to rediscover it."
What it is NOT: not a tooling change, not redoing existing work, not a finished system, not 776 work items to process.
The individual payoff: you know where a thing goes and who picks it up; fewer meetings, each with a written purpose; the feature is the unit we prioritise; the board reflects what's actually true.
The vision it serves, Erica verbatim: "intelligence in the flow of work" — human-agent teams delivering together, at clients and internally. And why this team goes first: "We're the change makers for the rest of the organization. If we can have intelligence in the flow of work, everyone else can too. But we need to start with us."

HARD LANGUAGE CONSTRAINT from Erica: never use "haphazard" or any wording that frames the old way as bad or unstructured — some people will hear it as personal criticism. The line is that the new way is what is now required, not that the old way was wrong. Keep it positive throughout.

Output should be a plan for a single-page infographic with three clear sequential sections reading as a journey (past → present → what it means for you).

args:
Render the blueprint below as a hand-drawn classroom sketchnote infographic. The blueprint is authoritative — do not add content, do not invent facts, do not reword the quoted fragments.

TITLE: What's in it for me?
SUBTITLE: Inform Digital — ways of working

CENTRAL VISUAL: A left-to-right rising path in three stages, drawn as a widening channel. Starts narrow (internal IT), broadens (client work added), opens into a structured lane with guide-rails running ALONGSIDE the direction of travel — never gates across it. The rails are the visual argument.

LAYOUT: Three horizontal bands, top to bottom, left-to-right within each band.

=== BAND 1 — WHERE WE'VE BEEN ===

MODULE 1 "Where we've been" / label: Grown up, grown in size
- We've evolved, we've grown up          [emphasise: We've evolved]
- Grown in size                           [emphasise: in size]
- Started as a team doing internal IT     [emphasise: internal IT]
- The work was real, the remit was narrower
Visual: narrow channel, single lane, small team icon. Solid and steady — draw as a foundation, never as a mess.

MODULE 2 "What we do now" / label: Four things at once
- We deliver client work                              [emphasise: client work]
- Asked to deliver frontier firm technology           [emphasise: frontier firm technology]
- We continue to support the business                 [emphasise: continue to support the business]
- Built tools for MoD that might become products      [emphasise: tools for MoD]
Visual: the channel splits into four coloured lanes running side by side, all flowing the same way. Visibly more than Module 1's single lane.

MODULE 3 "The shift, stated plainly" / label: So much more than we were
- From a team that does internal IT                   [emphasise: internal IT]
- To a capability delivering quality engineering to clients   [emphasise: quality engineering to clients]
- We are so much more than we were                    [emphasise whole line]
Visual: one bold arrow spanning beneath Modules 1 and 2, captioned before → after. This is the headline of the page.

=== BAND 2 — WHERE WE ARE NOW ===

MODULE 4 "Live now: strategy and roadmap" / label: Everyone gets a say
- Digital strategy and roadmap kicking off now   [emphasise: kicking off now]
- The whole team inputs — not a select few       [emphasise: The whole team inputs]
- You'll be asked: biggest governance constraints [emphasise: governance constraints]
- You'll be asked: what keeps you up at night     [emphasise: what keeps you up at night]
Visual: arrows pointing INWARD to a central roadmap shape, one per team member. Input, not broadcast.

MODULE 5 "What this is not" / label: Four things to put down
- Not a regime change — just getting better at what we do  [emphasise: Not a regime change]
- Not a tooling change                                      [emphasise: tooling change]
- Not redoing existing work                                 [emphasise: redoing]
- Not a finished system, not 776 items to process           [emphasise: finished system]
Visual: four items in a lightly struck-through row, set apart in their own bordered box. Deliberately visually quiet — anxiety being set down, not argued with. Place to the RIGHT of Module 4.

=== BAND 3 — WHAT IT MEANS FOR ME ===

MODULE 6 "Guardrails, not gates" / label: The operating principle
- Guardrails rather than gates                        [emphasise: Guardrails rather than gates]
- Enough structure to be predictable and professional [emphasise: predictable and professional]
- Freedom to think, adapt, improve                    [emphasise: think, adapt, improve]
- Not rules because people can't be trusted           [emphasise: Not rules because people can't be trusted]
- Capturing what we learned so nobody rediscovers it  [emphasise: nobody rediscovers it]
Example callout: "A gate stops you and asks permission. A guardrail lets you go faster."
Visual: direct contrast — a barrier ACROSS the lane (crossed out) beside rails ALONG it (ticked). Most important image on the page after the centre.

MODULE 7 "What you get" / label: Four concrete returns
- Know where a thing goes and who picks it up    [emphasise: where a thing goes]
- Fewer meetings, each with a written purpose     [emphasise: Fewer meetings]
- The feature is the unit we prioritise           [emphasise: feature]
- The board reflects what's actually true         [emphasise: what's actually true]
Visual: four payoff cards, each with a small glyph — a labelled tray, a shrinking calendar, a single highlighted card, a board matching reality. Most personally-addressed module on the page.

MODULE 8 "Why us, why first" / label: Intelligence in the flow of work
- Intelligence in the flow of work            [emphasise whole line]
- Human-agent teams delivering together       [emphasise: Human-agent teams]
- At clients, and internally
- We're the change makers for the rest of the organisation  [emphasise: We're the change makers]
- We need to start with us                    [emphasise: start with us]
Visual: the path opens outward at the far right into the wider organisation — several fainter paths branching from ours. Ours drawn first and solid; theirs follow.

TONE: Warm, confident, forward-looking. Every backward-looking line reads as growth. NOTHING may imply the old way was wrong, bad or disorganised — Module 1 is a foundation, Module 5 removes fear rather than assigning blame. Never use the word "haphazard" or any synonym.
